```{r setup}
# the bench files expect the repository root as working directory
setwd(params$root)
for (f in setdiff(Sys.glob("bench/*.R"), c("bench/cli.R", "bench/tests.R"))) {
  source(f)
}
rows <- bench_read_rows(params$rows)
measured <- rows[is.na(rows$skipped) & is.na(rows$error), ]
ops <- intersect(names(bench_ops()), unique(measured$op))
# one panel row per three cells
height <- function(op) 2 + 4 * ceiling(length(unique(.bench_cell_label(measured[measured$op == op, ]))) / 3)
# one tab per op: what it times, then its plot
op_tabs <- function(what) {
  for (op in ops) {
    cat("\n### ", op, "\n\n", BENCH_OP_DESCRIPTIONS[[op]], "\n\n", sep = "")
    cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(
      sprintf("```{r %s-%s, fig.width = 14, fig.height = %g}", what, op, height(op)),
      sprintf("bench_plot_cells(measured[measured$op == '%s', ], '%s')", op, what),
      "```"
    ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE))
  }
}
```

Results from ``r basename(params$rows)``, compared against **`r params$baseline`**.

## Summary

```{r summary}
#| output: asis
# the text report without its title, its headings one level down
md <- bench_report(rows, params$baseline)
md <- md[!grepl("^# ", md)]
cat(sub("^(#+) ", "\\1## ", md), sep = "\n")
```

## Time per cell

Seconds per call of the operation, one box per ref with every timed call as a point.
Setup, such as fitting the forest before `predict`, is not timed.
A cross marks results that kept only the median, minimum and maximum of their calls.

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r time}
#| output: asis
op_tabs("time")
```

:::

## Memory per cell

The highest memory the measuring R process used while the operation ran, one point per round.
This includes everything already in memory: the data, and for `predict`, `purify` and `predict_components` the forest their setup fitted.
The dashed line is the level after setup (of the round where it was lowest), so the distance from the line to the box is roughly what the operation itself added.
That distance can look smaller than the operation's real need, because it reuses memory the setup freed.
The text report's memory verdicts compare this distance, the plots show the whole peak.

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r memory}
#| output: asis
op_tabs("memory")
```

:::

## Scaling

Medians per ref and setting, both axes logarithmic.
Only settings measured at more than one size are shown.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Time over training rows

The prediction ops predict the same number of rows at every training size, and the forest's size is set by `n_splits`, not by the training rows.
Their time should therefore stay roughly flat here: see the predicted rows tabs for how prediction scales.

```{r scaling-time-n, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 10}
bench_plot_scaling(measured, "time", over = "n")
```

### Memory over training rows

Whole peak of the R process, as in the memory plots above.

```{r scaling-memory-n, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 10}
bench_plot_scaling(measured, "memory", over = "n")
```

### Time over predicted rows

`predict` and `predict_components` on one fitted forest, with an increasing number of rows to predict.

```{r scaling-time-new, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 6}
bench_plot_scaling(measured, "time", over = "n_new")
```

### Memory over predicted rows

```{r scaling-memory-new, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 6}
bench_plot_scaling(measured, "memory", over = "n_new")
```

:::
